properties.xtb_cross_check: GFN2-xTB (xtb 6.5.0), separate string entry, NOT averaged and NOT usable for the energy: FOOF r(F-O) = 1.518 A (1.5175), r(O-O) = 1.211 A (1.2106), E = -17.320490940487 Eh, ZPE = 0.0085164 Eh; FOO radical r(O-O) = 1.194 A, r(O-F) = 1.563 A, E = -12.612623952 Eh, ZPE = 0.0059846 Eh (3 real modes 446/652/1529 cm-1); F atom E = -4.619339964238 Eh, ZPE = 0. Balanced FOOF -> F + FOO: De = 55.55 kcal/mol, D0 = 53.96 kcal/mol, i.e. ~42 kcal/mol TOO HIGH (4x the 12-13 kcal/mol reference, 4.7x the PM7 value). GFN2 therefore fails on the energy but is informative on the shape of the coordinate: its constrained scan rises smoothly and plateaus at 54.2-54.3 kcal/mol for r(F1-O2) = 4.0-4.3 A, matching its component-based De, i.e. it reaches the F + FOO asymptote without a maximum.
properties.experimental_reference: microwave structure r(O-O) = 1.217 A, r(O-F) = 1.575 A, F-O-O 109.5 deg, dihedral 87.5 deg (experimental geometry anchor). The D0(F-O) value of 12-13 kcal/mol quoted in the task brief is the USER-SUPPLIED target, not an independently sourced number; the computed PM7 value 11.46 kcal/mol agrees with it within ~1 kcal/mol. No literature dHf(FOO,g) source is available inside this project, so no experimental BDE anchor is claimed beyond the user brief.
properties.method_bias: PM7 shortens the weak F-O bond by ~0.09 A (1.485 vs 1.575 A experimental) while reproducing r(O-O) essentially exactly (1.211 vs 1.217 A); the F-O length is therefore a lower bound on the true value
properties.xtb_note: Independent GFN2-xTB scan of the F1-O2 coordinate (calc/xtb/FOOF_scan/, closed-shell singlet continuous and monotonic 1.20-2.80 A rising to 44.4 kcal/mol, restricted SCF failure beyond, unrestricted doublet points 3.9-4.3 A flat at 54.1-54.3 kcal/mol matching the F + FOO asymptote): no point above the asymptote, so no barrier on the GFN2 surface either. The 3.1-3.8 A restricted points are SCF artifacts and are not used.

properties.note: fluorooxy (FO2) radical, the counter-fragment of the balanced first F-O cleavage; doublet minimum (charge 0, multiplicity 2, <S**2> = 0.7616). PM7 makes it strongly asymmetric: r(O-O) = 1.128 A, r(O-F) = 1.540 A. The 1.500/1.500 A geometry quoted in an earlier review is the input geometry (2D RDKit seed), not the converged structure.

properties.note: fluorine atom, single point; a one-atom species has no vibrational modes so its ZPE is exactly 0

Dissociation asymptote F + FOO. It is NOT a stationary point at the allowed level of theory: from r(F-O) = 4.200 A an unconstrained PM7 opt+freq collapses back to covalent FOOF (NImag = 0), from the 4.235 A scan endpoint it collapses to a compact F-O-O isomer (E = 0.00640994 Eh, +1.5 kcal/mol above FOOF, NImag = 0), and the rigid 4.200 A point has one -62.0 cm-1 imaginary mode; the restricted closed-shell SCF also fails to converge at long range. The asymptote energy is therefore built from the separately optimized fragments (FOO minimum + F atom single point), which is the standard bond-energy protocol and the route the task brief allows for a complex that is not a clean minimum.

edges.channel: F-O homolysis from the terminal oxygen: no first-order saddle found along the relaxed F-O coordinate
edges.note: No first-order saddle was found along the relaxed F-O coordinate. The relaxed PM7 scan shows no maximum above its own boundary point (calc/pm7scan/FOOF_scan_cont_4p04_4p23.log; +74.3 kcal/mol at 4.235 A), but the restricted PM7 surface rearranges instead of dissociating (a 4.200 A start relaxes back to covalent FOOF, NImag = 0; the 4.235 A start relaxes to a compact F-O-O isomer 1.5 kcal/mol above FOOF, NImag = 0; the rigid 4.200 A point has one -62.0 cm-1 mode). The GFN2-xTB scan of the same coordinate does reach the asymptote: it rises smoothly and plateaus at 54.2-54.3 kcal/mol for r = 4.0-4.3 A, matching the component-based GFN2 De of 55.55 kcal/mol, with no maximum above the plateau. Conclusion: barrierless homolysis, no saddle on either allowed surface; therefore no TS node, no via target, no barrier_kcal_mol, and the ts_opt / imaginary-frequency / short_irc stages are not applicable. The F-O bond dissociation energy is built from the separately optimized fragments.
